# **gaiaDocker**

## Description

gaiaDocker provides **containerized deployment orchestration** for the complete Gaia toolchain. It coordinates image builds, manages versioned releases, and enables consistent deployment across development, testing, and production environments.

## Key Features

- **Complete stack deployment** with a single command
- **Profile-based configuration** (gaia, degauss) for flexible deployments
- **Coordinated versioning** across all Gaia components
- **Persistent data storage** for databases and search indexes
- **Service orchestration** via Docker Compose
- **OHDSI Broadsea integration** for broader ecosystem compatibility

## Services Managed

gaiaDocker orchestrates the following services:
- **gaia-db**: PostgreSQL/PostGIS database (gaiaDB)
- **gaia-core**: RStudio with HADES and the gaiaCore R package (image `ohdsi/gaia-core`)
- **gaia-postgrest**: optional PostgREST API service
- **gaia-catalog**: Flask catalog interface
- **gaia-solr**: Solr search engine
- **gaia-osgeo**: GDAL/OGR ETL tools
- **gaia-postgis**: PostGIS-specific ETL tools
- **gaia-degauss** (optional): Geocoding service

## Platforms

The reference deployment uses Docker Compose. It has been deployed on Linux and macOS, and a default Windows 11 deployment has run the tutorial pipeline. It needs Docker, Docker Compose and about 50 GB of free storage (more if you add geocoding reference data). Docker is a convenience, not a requirement: gaiaDB is a standard PostgreSQL/PostGIS database that runs on any native Postgres server, and gaiaCore can be pointed at any gaiaDB instance.

## Quick Start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/OHDSI/gaiaDocker.git
cd gaiaDocker
docker compose --profile gaia up -d
```

## Pinned images for the tutorial

For the tutorial, a Compose override file pins the services of the `gaia` profile (database, PostgREST, catalog, Solr and pgAdmin) to specific image versions so everyone runs exactly the same stack. See [Get Started](get-started.html) for the command and the [tutorial checklist](tutorial.html) for the pinned R image.
